name: Better Place
one_liner: EV charging and battery-swap network that leased batteries to drivers of swappable electric cars.
story: Founded by ex-SAP executive Shai Agassi, Better Place was formally US-based but ran its main operations in Israel, aiming to make EVs cheaper than gasoline cars by owning the batteries and swapping them in minutes at robotic stations; it raised roughly $850M from investors including Israel Corp., HSBC, Morgan Stanley, GE and UBS, peaking at a $2.25B post-money private valuation in its 2011 Series C. Only one car, the Renault Fluence Z.E., ever supported its swap system and other automakers such as Tesla saw no reason to build swappable packs, so after Agassi was ousted in late 2012 the company filed for bankruptcy in Israel on 26 May 2013 and receivers sold the remaining assets in November 2013 for about $450,000.

near_death.what: Founder-CEO Shai Agassi was ousted about seven months before the bankruptcy as Renault Fluence sales in Israel fell far short of plan.

dismissed_by.quote_or_fact: Paraphrase: most EV makers, Tesla included, saw no reason to build or install swappable batteries, leaving Better Place dependent on a single Renault model.

name: Solyndra
one_liner: Maker of cylindrical CIGS thin-film solar panels designed for flat commercial rooftops.
story: Solyndra bet that tube-shaped CIGS panels would beat conventional silicon on rooftops, raised close to $1 billion of private equity (backers included Argonaut and the Walton-linked Madrone) and in 2009 won the first Recovery Act loan guarantee, $535 million (about $527 million drawn), to build a new Fremont factory; total raised here sums ~$1B private plus the drawn DOE loan. Its December 2009 IPO filing came with auditor going-concern doubts and was pulled in June 2010 in favor of $175 million of notes from existing investors, and as silicon panel prices collapsed it filed for bankruptcy on 1 September 2011, laying off about 1,100 workers and becoming a political symbol of the stimulus (DOJ declined criminal charges in 2015).

near_death.what: IPO registered in December 2009 was withdrawn in June 2010 after its S-1 audit flagged recurring losses and substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern; it raised $175M in notes from existing investors instead of the ~$300M sought.

dismissed_by.quote_or_fact: Paraphrase: the audit cited recurring operating losses, negative cash flows since inception and a stockholders' deficit that raised substantial doubt about Solyndra's ability to continue as a going concern.

name: Northvolt
one_liner: Swedish lithium-ion battery maker building gigafactories to give Europe its own green EV-battery champion.
story: Co-founded by ex-Tesla executive Peter Carlsson, Northvolt set out to build Europe's answer to Asian battery giants with a flagship gigafactory (Northvolt Ett) in Skellefteå, raising more than $14 billion in equity, debt and public funding (Sifted counts about EUR 15bn) from backers led by Volkswagen (about 21%) and Goldman Sachs. With liquidity described as dire in its own petition and roughly $5.8bn of debt, it filed for US Chapter 11 on 21 November 2024 as Carlsson resigned, then filed for bankruptcy in Sweden in March 2025; US startup Lyten agreed in August 2025 to buy the remaining Swedish and German plants and IP for undisclosed terms. Peak private valuation was not confirmed in sources checked, so it is left null.

near_death.what: Filed for Chapter 11 in the Southern District of Texas on 21 Nov 2024 with about $145M of cash collateral and $100M of DIP financing; co-founder and CEO Peter Carlsson resigned; Volkswagen and Goldman Sachs wrote down their stakes.
